items.summary: fix(memory-flush): fallback to estimatePromptTokensFromSessionTranscript when usage data is unavailable (#83178) * fix(memory-flush): fallback to estimatePromptTokensFromSessionTranscript when usage data is unavailable When a model provider (e.g., MiniMax) does not return usage data in its API response, the session entry's totalTokens stays undefined. The preflight compaction path already handles this via estimatePromptTokensFromSessionTranscript, but the memory-flush path did not have the same fallback. This caused entry.totalTokens to remain undefined across compactions, preventing the system from recognizing context reductions and triggering redundant compactions. This change adds the same fallback from the preflight path into the memory-flush path, ensuring entry.totalTokens is populated even when the model does not provide usage data. * fix(memory): flush context without provider token usage Use the transcript estimator for pre-compaction memory checkpoints while keeping heuristic totals out of persisted provider usage. Share output-once projection with compaction and preserve empty-history flush behavior. Fixes #83177. Co-authored-by: njuboy11 * test(memory): align flush fixtures with transcript owners --------- Co-authored-by: njuboy11 Co-authored-by: Peter Steinberger

items.summary: fix: model list builds slow down quadratically with large provider catalogs (#166223) * perf(models): skip unmatchable provider rows in runtime policy lookup resolveModelConfig scanned every authored row of the selected provider and parsed each row id to test for an exact match. Catalog projection resolves a runtime policy several times per row (harness policy, CLI runtime auth, catalog decision runtime, native evaluation), so a provider with N authored models cost O(N^2) ref parses per models.list build. With 402 rows this was the largest single cost in an uncached build. An exact match must end with the requested model id, so rows that do not are skipped before parsing. Matching semantics are unchanged; a table test pins self-qualified row matching that the prefilter relies on. * test(models): bound parsing work for large provider catalogs --------- Co-authored-by: Peter Steinberger

items.title: perf(control-ui): preload native plugin assets together (#168059)
items.summary: perf(control-ui): preload native plugin assets together (#168059) Control UI plugin entry modules, their static imports, and stylesheets are now preloaded as soon as the bootstrap config is known (including the config embedded in authenticated documents), CSS and JS load in parallel, and the plugin catalog RPC and config refresh run concurrently. The Gateway records each plugin revision's static browser imports once per snapshot. A plugin catalog failure leaves bootstrap identity and document delivery intact (empty plugin list); the plugins.controlUi.list RPC remains the owner that reports catalog errors.

items.title: test(agents): match compatible Responses runtime carrier shape
items.summary: test(agents): match compatible Responses runtime carrier shape Align provider-review continuation request captures with #168546. The ChatGPT Responses fixture is outside the native OpenAI endpoint predicate, so its runtime carrier keeps the user role and original content blocks. Keep the exact reviewed steer, carrier ordering, image omission, request count, transcript immutability and review-settlement assertions. This only updates two expected arrays; no request assembly or provider policy changes. Linux proof: 32 focused tests, all 1,454 tests in the original 111-file shard, and 11 provider-role tests pass. Restoring unconditional instruction role conversion makes all four affected cases fail. Selected test types, lint and P2 review pass. The unrelated dead-export failures also reproduce on the untouched baseline; no ignores or suppressions were changed.
